description: Domain security reconnaissance MCP server — 30 tools for AI agents, also usable from the command line (npx dechonet-mcp ssl example.com). Phishing/smishing link checks, external exposure maps, DNS, SSL, post-quantum TLS readiness, HTTP headers, email auth
author: DechoNet

tool_signatures.name: asm_nuclei_cancel
tool_signatures.description: Stop new requests and terminate this workspace scanner with edit permission. Already transmitted requests cannot be recalled. Poll for cancellation acknowledgement.

tool_signatures.name: asm_nuclei_start
tool_signatures.description: Explicitly start limited active requests to a selected currently verified asset in your owned ASM report. Requires current workspace edit access, ASM plan and current account-bound DNS TXT ownership (legacy public/domain-only proof is insufficient); public API keys grant no account authority. No exploits or arbitrary templates/CLI.

tool_signatures.name: asm_nuclei_status
tool_signatures.description: Read private job status, coverage and sanitized evidence with current view permission and ownership. Partial, failed or unconfigured is not a clean result; technology detection is not proof of a vulnerability.

tool_signatures.name: asn_lookup
tool_signatures.description: Look up Autonomous System (ASN) / BGP information for an IP address or AS number: the network operator, announced prefixes, abuse contact, and a classification (cloud, CDN, ISP, hosting, or enterprise). Use this to identify who runs a network or whether an IP is cloud/CDN-hosted. Use reverse_dns instead for the host-level PTR name of a single IP. Read-only; requires no API key; rate-limited. Returns operator, prefixes, classification, and abuse contact.

tool_signatures.name: case_kit_observe
tool_signatures.description: Explicitly observe an existing authenticated case member under conditional-render rules and daily cap. Requires edit access and current case owner session or access cookie. Search and page GET do not render; unavailable is not a clean result.

tool_signatures.name: case_kit_search
tool_signatures.description: Search render fingerprints within an authenticated case and allowed public discovery data. Requires the case owner session or existing case access cookie; public API keys do not grant case access. Screen, same-kit and operational candidates are distinct; scores are proximity, not probability, operator identity or phishing verdicts. Kits can be sold or copied.

tool_signatures.name: check_before_action
tool_signatures.description: Check the page an agent is about to log in, pay, download from or submit to: whether the address impersonates a brand, how new the domain is, whether DechoNet or a licensed feed has already flagged it, and — opened from Seoul (and Tokyo for Japan-targeted pages) as a phone — what the page turns into, including text it hides from people but an AI agent would read (instructions to ignore its rules, hand over secrets or keep the user out of it raise the answer to suspicious). For a payment, the caller can report the page structure as host names only (where forms submit, which origins frames come from, whether the card fields sit on the page itself or in a frame and that frame

tool_signatures.name: dns_lookup
tool_signatures.description: Query DNS records (A, AAAA, MX, TXT, NS, SOA, CAA) for a domain and validate email-related records, including DNSSEC presence and SPF/DMARC syntax, returning severity-rated diagnostics. Use this for a single authoritative answer about one domain. Use dns_propagation instead when you need to compare answers across multiple global resolvers (e.g., right after a change), or email_auth for a full SPF/DKIM/DMARC deliverability assessment. Read-only; requires no API key or authentication; subject to rate limiting. Returns a text report: status, KPI summary, detected issues, and recommended actions.

tool_signatures.name: dns_propagation
tool_signatures.description: Query one DNS record across 8+ global public resolvers (Google, Cloudflare, Quad9, OpenDNS, and more) simultaneously and report which resolvers return stale versus updated values. Use this after changing a record to confirm worldwide propagation. Use dns_lookup instead for a single authoritative answer with SPF/DMARC validation. Read-only; requires no API key; rate-limited. Returns per-resolver values and a consistency verdict.

tool_signatures.name: domain_changes
tool_signatures.description: Report what has changed for a domain over time — the security regressions and drift that DechoNet\

tool_signatures.name: domain_history
tool_signatures.description: Show how a domain\

tool_signatures.name: email_auth
tool_signatures.description: Assess a domain

tool_signatures.name: email_header_analysis
tool_signatures.description: Parse raw email headers to reconstruct the delivery path (each Received hop in order), extract SPF/DKIM/DMARC authentication results, measure per-hop delays, and flag unencrypted (non-TLS) hops. Use this to diagnose a specific message that was already delivered — spoofing, delays, or where mail was lost. Use email_auth instead to assess a domain\

tool_signatures.name: exposure_map
tool_signatures.description: Map what an organisation exposes to the internet beyond its home page: subdomains from Certificate Transparency logs (plus hosts DechoNet has already observed), each opened once from outside and sorted into developer/ops tools, directory listings, admin screens, VPN/remote-access logins, staging servers, default install pages, login pages and so on — the forgotten assets AI-driven attack tools look for first. Use this when a user wants to know their attack surface or after a breach in their sector. Returns counts per category, a verdict (bad/warn/ok) and what to do. Public view only: the per-host list and a sensitive-file check are shown to the verified domain owner on the web report (DNS TXT), never through this tool. Read-only and passive beyond a single first-page request per host; no logins or path guessing; requires no API key; rate-limited (heavier than other tools — up to ~1 minute).

tool_signatures.name: golive_check
tool_signatures.description: Check whether a domain is ready to launch or migrate — a go/no-go verdict over five essentials: DNS resolves to an IP, has propagated consistently across global resolvers, SSL/TLS is ready, the site is reachable over HTTPS, and the domain registration is not about to expire. Use this right before flipping DNS to a new server, or to confirm a migration has landed. It answers

tool_signatures.name: http_security
tool_signatures.description: Follow a URL

tool_signatures.name: impersonation_exposure
tool_signatures.description: Assess how exposed a domain is to brand impersonation and phishing, PASSIVELY: live typosquat/lookalike domains (homoglyph, omission, transposition, TLD swap) that actually resolve, operational subdomains (dev/staging/admin) exposed in CT logs, and whether a wildcard certificate exists — returning an A+ (low exposure) to F (high exposure) grade. Framing: a registered lookalike domain is not proof of impersonation — it may be a legitimate third party or the owner\

tool_signatures.name: infrastructure_pivot
tool_signatures.description: Find other domains DechoNet has seen with the same infrastructure value — a nameserver, IP address, MX host, certificate issuer or registrar — with first and last seen, to map related infrastructure (e.g. other phishing domains on the same rare nameserver). Use it after domain_history or dns_lookup gives you a distinctive value. Shared infrastructure (CDN edges, public CAs, large registrars and DNS hosts) returns a count only, since sharing it says nothing about ownership. Read-only; REQUIRES a free DechoNet API key (account page; remote: send Authorization: Bearer dn_…, npm: set DECHONET_API_KEY); up to 20 rows per call (higher for some keys); rate-limited. Coverage: only DechoNet\

tool_signatures.name: ip_info
tool_signatures.description: Report information about the caller

tool_signatures.name: lookalike_domains
tool_signatures.description: Generate the typosquat/lookalike variants of a domain that phishers actually register — homoglyph swaps (l→1, o→0, rn→m), TLD swaps (.com→.co), character omissions, transpositions, repetitions, hyphenations — and check which of them are currently registered (live NS delegation via DoH). Use this to assess brand-impersonation and phishing exposure for a domain the user is responsible for. A registered variant is NOT proof of abuse (it may be an unrelated legitimate site) — follow up with whois_lookup on each hit for its owner and registration date. Read-only; requires no API key; rate-limited. Returns generated/checked counts and the registered variants with the technique that produced each.

tool_signatures.name: mcp_server_check
tool_signatures.description: Check a remote MCP server from outside before connecting it to an agent: whether it requires authentication (and publishes OAuth protected-resource metadata, RFC 9728), which of its tools act on the world (run commands, write or delete files, send messages, make payments, read secrets), whether its server instructions or tool and parameter descriptions contain text that steers an agent (tool poisoning), whether a web page on any site could call it (CORS and Origin), HTTPS, and tool annotations. Sends initialize and tools/list only — no tool is ever called; query strings are removed before anything is sent or stored. Public addresses only. Findings cover what the server shows from outside: what a tool does when called, the server code and tools behind a login are not checked and are listed as not checked. Read-only; requires no API key; rate-limited. Returns status, KPIs, issues, actions, what was not checked, and a shareable report link.

tool_signatures.name: owasp_check
tool_signatures.description: Assess a domain

tool_signatures.name: phishing_link_check
tool_signatures.description: Check the links in a suspicious text message (smishing) or e-mail before anyone taps them. Paste the whole message or a single URL: every link is extracted, followed through URL shorteners to its real destination, and judged on observable signals — domain age from RDAP, impersonation of Korean banks/couriers/telecoms/portals and global brands incl. AI services such as ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini (brand keyword, lookalike spelling, or the brand domain worn as a subdomain), ClickFix pages (a fake

tool_signatures.name: port_scan
tool_signatures.description: Probe a host for a fixed set of common TCP ports (HTTP, HTTPS, SSH, FTP, SMTP, DNS, and common databases) and report which are open, the service name, and the response time. BEHAVIOR: this makes an ACTIVE TCP connection to the target. It is non-intrusive — a connect probe only; it does not authenticate, send exploits, or transfer data — and changes nothing on the target (read-only), but the connection is visible in the target\

tool_signatures.name: pqc_readiness
tool_signatures.description: Check whether a website\

tool_signatures.name: report_page
tool_signatures.description: Report a page to DechoNet: phishing or brand impersonation, a fake payment window (card fields where a payment provider should be), hidden instructions aimed at AI agents, a malicious download, a DechoNet verdict that looks wrong (false_positive) or a danger it missed (missed), an MCP server whose tool descriptions steer agents (malicious_mcp — url is the MCP endpoint), or a network anomaly (network_anomaly — the certificate serial/issuer or addresses you saw for the host, in observed). Kept for 90 days: the host and the kind, with an anonymous reporter hash used to count independent reports; for malicious_mcp the endpoint path, for network_anomaly the observed values and the country of the connection. No query, page text or free text. A report changes no verdict by itself: DechoNet opens the page itself and only what it observes counts; pages reported by several independent sources are looked at first. Not read-only (it records the report); rate-limited.

tool_signatures.name: reverse_dns
tool_signatures.description: Resolve the PTR (reverse DNS) record for an IPv4 or IPv6 address and verify forward-confirmed reverse DNS (FCrDNS) by checking that the PTR hostname resolves back to the same IP. Infers the hosting provider from PTR naming patterns. Use this to validate mail-server rDNS or identify a single IP\

tool_signatures.name: security_scan
tool_signatures.description: One-shot comprehensive audit of a domain, scored 0-100 with an A+ to F grade and a prioritized action list. Five scored areas: the web connection (TLS certificate and HTTP security headers, measured on www when only www has an address), mail spoofing defence (SPF/DKIM/DMARC; a domain that uses no mail is judged only on SPF -all and an enforced DMARC policy), domain registration and DNS, exposure (admin screens, developer tools and the like on hosts named in public certificate logs — counts only), and reputation (DechoNet verdict store and licensed phishing feeds). DNS propagation, reverse DNS and ASN are returned as reference information and not scored. A warning costs a quarter of its area and a critical half; data that could not be read in full is flagged, not charged, and an exposure or reputation lookup that fails is reported as not checked. Call the individual tools (e.g., ssl_check, email_auth, exposure_map) for depth on one area. BEHAVIOR: passive — public lookups and ordinary HTTPS requests only; open ports are NOT scanned (port_scan is the separate, active check). Takes up to about a minute (the exposure lookup). Read-only; requires no API key; rate-limited (it makes multiple backend calls). Returns the score, per-area breakdown, reference areas, top actions, and per-area summaries.

tool_signatures.name: set_expectations
tool_signatures.description: Record what a domain should show from outside and check it now — HSTS or another header present, DMARC enforcing, an issue key no longer reported, an HTTP or TLS grade at or above a level, a certificate with enough days left, a DNS record present, absent or containing a value, HTTPS answering. DechoNet reads the domain fresh (not from cache) with its public dns / ssl / http / email tools, from its own servers and the Seoul observation point, and then re-checks the set every day. Each result is pass, fail or unknown; unknown (a tool or part of it did not answer) is never a pass. Without an API key the set is anonymous: no alerts, kept 30 days after its last check, reachable by id and status page. With an API key (Authorization: Bearer dn_…) the set belongs to that key

tool_signatures.name: ssl_check
tool_signatures.description: Inspect a host

tool_signatures.name: subdomain_discovery
tool_signatures.description: Enumerate the subdomains of a domain from Certificate Transparency logs — fully passive (no packets are sent to the target; CT logs are public records of every TLS certificate ever issued). Flags operational-looking names (dev, staging, admin, vpn, legacy) and wildcard certificates, because forgotten subdomains are a common takeover path. Use this as the first recon step to map a domain

tool_signatures.name: subnet_calc
tool_signatures.description: Compute IPv4 subnet details from CIDR notation entirely locally — no network call: network and broadcast addresses, usable host range, total usable hosts, subnet mask, and wildcard mask. /31 and /32 are handled per RFC 3021 (point-to-point / single host). Use this for IPv4 address planning. It does not query DNS or contact any host, so it is purely computational. Requires no API key and is NOT rate-limited (computed in-process). Returns the calculated fields as text.

tool_signatures.name: verify_expectations
tool_signatures.description: Check expectations from outside now, with fresh reads: either a stored set by id (from set_expectations — its state is updated and an anonymous set is kept another 30 days), or a domain plus a list of checks once, storing nothing. Same checks and outcomes as set_expectations (pass / fail / unknown, unknown is never a pass), each tool read once with a signed observation receipt. Typical use: right after a change, to see whether it is visible from outside yet — DNS and CDN changes can take minutes to hours to show. Rate-limited (a few checks per minute).

tool_signatures.name: watch_domain
tool_signatures.description: Start (or reuse) a daily DechoNet watch on a domain so that changes are recorded over time — SSL grade/issuer/expiry, DNS records, HTTP security headers, domain registration, and optionally OWASP posture and impersonation exposure. Use this once when the user cares about a domain beyond a one-off check (their own domain, a client, a vendor, a target under investigation). After this, domain_changes answers

tool_signatures.name: whois_lookup
tool_signatures.description: Retrieve domain registration data via RDAP (with WHOIS fallback): registrar, creation/expiry/update dates, nameservers, and EPP status flags, highlighting risk states such as clientHold and pendingDelete. Use this for ownership, lifecycle, and expiry questions about a registered domain. Use dns_lookup instead for live DNS records, or reverse_dns/asn_lookup for IP-level ownership. Read-only; requires no API key; rate-limited. Returns registrar, key dates, nameservers, and status flags.

Without an API key the set is anonymous: no alerts, kept 30 days after its last check, reachable by id and status page. With an API key (Authorization: Bearer dn_…) the set belongs to that key

tool_signatures.name: ssl_check
tool_signatures.description: Inspect a host

tool_signatures.name: subdomain_discovery
tool_signatures.description: Enumerate the subdomains of a domain from Certificate Transparency logs — fully passive (no packets are sent to the target; CT logs are public records of every TLS certificate ever issued). Flags operational-looking names (dev, staging, admin, vpn, legacy) and wildcard certificates, because forgotten subdomains are a common takeover path. Use this as the first recon step to map a domain

tool_signatures.name: subnet_calc
tool_signatures.description: Compute IPv4 subnet details from CIDR notation entirely locally — no network call: network and broadcast addresses, usable host range, total usable hosts, subnet mask, and wildcard mask. /31 and /32 are handled per RFC 3021 (point-to-point / single host). Use this for IPv4 address planning. It does not query DNS or contact any host, so it is purely computational. Requires no API key and is NOT rate-limited (computed in-process). Returns the calculated fields as text.

tool_signatures.name: verify_expectations
tool_signatures.description: Check expectations from outside now, with fresh reads: either a stored set by id (from set_expectations — its state is updated and an anonymous set is kept another 30 days), or a domain plus a list of checks once, storing nothing. Same checks and outcomes as set_expectations (pass / fail / unknown, unknown is never a pass), each tool read once with a signed observation receipt. Typical use: right after a change, to see whether it is visible from outside yet — DNS and CDN changes can take minutes to hours to show. Rate-limited (a few checks per minute).

tool_signatures.name: watch_domain
tool_signatures.description: Start (or reuse) a daily DechoNet watch on a domain so that changes are recorded over time — SSL grade/issuer/expiry, DNS records, HTTP security headers, domain registration, and optionally OWASP posture and impersonation exposure. Use this once when the user cares about a domain beyond a one-off check (their own domain, a client, a vendor, a target under investigation). After this, domain_changes answers

tool_signatures.name: whois_lookup
tool_signatures.description: Retrieve domain registration data via RDAP (with WHOIS fallback): registrar, creation/expiry/update dates, nameservers, and EPP status flags, highlighting risk states such as clientHold and pendingDelete. Use this for ownership, lifecycle, and expiry questions about a registered domain. Use dns_lookup instead for live DNS records, or reverse_dns/asn_lookup for IP-level ownership. Read-only; requires no API key; rate-limited. Returns registrar, key dates, nameservers, and status flags.
